extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders, regulated entities, advocates, and members of the public who may submit comments or petitions in Federal Trade Commission rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural notices about FTC proposed rules and petitions, describing what the Commission invites from the public (written comments, data, argument, requests for oral presentation) and what kinds of information the Commission seeks in rule reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to submit written comments on petitions for rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Please take notice that the Federal Trade Commission ("Commission") received a petition for rulemaking ... The Commission invites written comments concerning the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication of the petition is pursuant to the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure; publication does not affect the legal status of the petition or its final disposition. Commenters should submit written comments addressing the petition's requests and claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include data and argument concerning the need for rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission is soliciting written comment, data, and argument concerning the need for such a rulemaking to prevent persons, entities, and organizations from engaging in such unfair or deceptive acts or practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should present factual evidence, empirical data, or reasoned argument demonstrating whether a rule is needed (or not), the scope of the problem, and why regulatory action is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide evidence on prevalence and lifecycle-specific practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission is soliciting written comment, including data and argument, concerning such fees and charges throughout a lease lifecycle, from application to move out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appropriate, commenters should document how practices occur across different stages (e.g., application, tenancy, move-out), provide statistics or case examples, and explain prevalence and consumer impact at each stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address economic impact, benefits, and conflicts with other laws
rubrics_metrics.description: In each rule review, the Commission requests public comments on, among other things, the economic impact and benefits of the rule; possible conflict between the rule and state, local, or other federal laws or regulations; and the effect on the rule of any technological, economic, or other industry changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should include analyses of costs and benefits, quantification where possible, identification of any legal or regulatory conflicts, and discussion of how technological or market changes affect the rule's necessity or design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide information on small-entity impacts per the Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The RFA requires publication in the Federal Register of agenda entries for rules that are likely to have a significant impact on a substantial number of small entities ... The Commission has identified rulemakings that are likely to have some impact on small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a rule may affect small businesses or other small entities, commenters should provide evidence on the number and types of small entities affected, magnitude of impacts, and possible mitigations or alternatives to reduce burdens on small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propose clear drafting changes and address vagueness or scienter requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: This petition requests to clarify and remove vague terms for precise enforcement of the plan regulations and the inclusion of a scienter requirement to safeguard consumers and businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments may recommend specific textual edits, highlight vague language, argue for or against scienter (knowledge) requirements, and explain how drafting changes would affect enforceability and consumer protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to specific proposed amendments and scope changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The SNPRM requested additional public comment on whether the Commission should revise the title of the Rule, add a prohibition on the impersonation of individuals, and extend liability for violations of the Rule to parties who provide goods and services with knowledge or reason to know that those goods or services will be used in impersonation schemes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the agency requests comment on particular proposed changes, commenters should take explicit positions on those proposals, provide supporting evidence or legal analysis, and offer alternative formulations or approaches where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide evidence of consumer harm and justification for remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed amendment is necessary in light of the widespread deception and consumer injury caused by tech support scams. The amendment would provide the Commission with the ability to obtain stronger relief in cases involving tech support scams, including civil penalties and consumer redress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments supporting remedial measures should document the nature and scale of harms, supply examples or data on consumer injury, and discuss which remedies (penalties, redress, scope of coverage) are proportional and effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request and prepare for oral presentations or informal hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: The SNPRM announced the opportunity for interested parties to present their positions orally at an informal hearing. Six commenters requested to participate at the informal hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested parties may request to present oral comments; follow the Commission's procedures for requesting participation and prepare concise, well-supported oral statements that align with your written comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe comment deadlines and monitor for extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission is extending the deadline for filing comments on its Notice of Proposed Rulemaking ("NPRM").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submissions are timely. Monitor Federal Register notices for extensions or changes to deadlines; late submissions may not be considered unless extensions are granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat regulatory agenda projections as staff judgments, not final determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for notice of completed actions, the information in this agenda represents the judgment of Commission staff ... No final determination by the staff or the Commission respecting the need for or the substance of a rule should be inferred from the notation of projected events in this agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use agenda listings to understand likely activity and timing, but do not assume listed items reflect final Commission decisions; tailor comments and planning accordingly.
